title: "Provenance" module (FAIR, RO-Crate, ISA, ELN concepts)
context: Provenance — recording how a result was produced — is required for reproducibility and is now mandated by major funders (NIH, journal data/code-availability requirements). Cancer researchers lack training in metadata standards, the FAIR principles, RO-Crate, the ISA metadata framework, and electronic lab notebooks at a level that makes provenance machine-readable and auditable. The module targets non-computational scientists and teaches these concepts without requiring prior informatics knowledge. Depends on: template-004, container-ci-005.
objective: Author the 'Provenance' module covering FAIR principles, RO-Crate, ISA metadata framework, and electronic lab notebook concepts following the module template, with 3-6 Bloom-aligned learning objectives, a runnable pinned-container exercise using synthetic data, checklist/takeaway, formative assessment, and instructor notes; CI green; signed off by Educator and Domain reviewers.
acceptanceCriteria: Module follows the template: 3-6 Bloom-aligned learning objectives, lesson narrative with all assertions cited, runnable pinned-container exercise using synthetic data, checklist/takeaway, formative assessment, and instructor notes.

Teaches FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable), RO-Crate (Research Object Crate) for packaging provenance metadata, ISA (Investigation/Study/Assay) metadata framework, and ELN concepts at a conceptual level suitable for bench scientists.
Hands-on exercise creates a minimal RO-Crate or ISA-structured metadata record for a synthetic dataset; runs in a pinned container and passes CI (Docker + Apptainer); no raw cancer data committed.
No biological/clinical conclusion presented as a finding.
All lesson assertions cited; link/citation checker passes in CI.
Reviewed and signed off by Educator reviewer and Domain reviewer; DCO signed off.
resources: FAIR Guiding Principles (Wilkinson et al., 2016, https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18)
output: A complete 'Provenance' module committed to the project repo (lesson, exercise with synthetic data, checklist, assessment, instructor notes) with CI green (Docker + Apptainer) and Educator + Domain reviewer sign-offs.
